# Mythos Atlas

> https://mythosatlas.com — Interactive world mythology encyclopedia (deities, stories, pantheons, creatures, artifacts, locations, quizzes, timelines, family trees).

## Summary

Mythos Atlas is a research-oriented reference and learning site for ancient and world mythology. Content is curated into structured entries with cross-links, maps, knowledge graphs, and study tools (quizzes, spaced repetition, learning paths). The site is built with Next.js; all content is served from versioned static JSON.

## URL aliases

- [/domains](https://mythosatlas.com/domains) redirects to [/divine-domains](https://mythosatlas.com/divine-domains) (canonical hub for domains of influence).

## Primary entry points

- [Home](https://mythosatlas.com/): the atlas landing page.
- [Browse deities](https://mythosatlas.com/deities): every deity entry.
- [Browse stories](https://mythosatlas.com/stories): myth retellings and summaries.
- [Pantheons](https://mythosatlas.com/pantheons): the traditions covered.
- [Compare tools](https://mythosatlas.com/compare): cross-pantheon comparison, including [archetype parallels](https://mythosatlas.com/compare/parallels).
- [Knowledge graph](https://mythosatlas.com/knowledge-graph): relationship explorer.
- [Family tree explorer](https://mythosatlas.com/family-tree): divine genealogies.
- [Quizzes](https://mythosatlas.com/quiz): self-testing, plus [study guides](https://mythosatlas.com/study).
- [Sources](https://mythosatlas.com/sources) and [About](https://mythosatlas.com/about): citation standards and methodology.

## Guides

Editorial hubs that set a modern retelling or an ancient epic beside its sources, separating ancient material from modern invention and linking every figure and place to its entry.

- [All guides](https://mythosatlas.com/guides)
- [The Myths Behind Percy Jackson: The Titan's Curse](https://mythosatlas.com/guides/percy-jackson-titans-curse): Artemis and her Hunters, Atlas, Zoë Nightshade and the Hesperides, the Nemean Lion, Ladon, the Ophiotaurus, Mount Othrys and Kronos, each against Hesiod, Apollodorus, Apollonius and Ovid.
- [The Odyssey: A Guide to Homer's Epic](https://mythosatlas.com/guides/odyssey): Odysseus's route (Troy to Ithaca, with each stop classed as real, identified or mythic), a 24-book summary, and the cast. About Homer's poem, not any film.
- [Who's Who in Hades II](https://mythosatlas.com/guides/hades-ii): Melinoë (Orphic Hymn 71), Hecate, Chronos versus Cronus, Nyx and her children, Nemesis, Odysseus and Charon, with what the game invents.

## Gods by domain

- [Divine domains](https://mythosatlas.com/divine-domains) is the hub. Each domain held by at least three deities in two or more traditions has its own page at `/gods-of/<domain>`, for example [gods of war](https://mythosatlas.com/gods-of/war), [love](https://mythosatlas.com/gods-of/love), [the sea](https://mythosatlas.com/gods-of/sea), [death](https://mythosatlas.com/gods-of/death), [wisdom](https://mythosatlas.com/gods-of/wisdom) and [the sun](https://mythosatlas.com/gods-of/sun). Every name and description on those pages comes from the deity entries.
- Head-to-head pages at `/compare/<a>-vs-<b>` (index: [comparison pairs](https://mythosatlas.com/compare/pairs)) exist only for pairs the catalog links through a cross-pantheon parallel or a recorded kinship.
- Deity entries answer family questions (parents, children, consorts, siblings) from the catalog's kinship records, which are not exhaustive.

## Machine-readable sitemap

- [sitemap.xml](https://mythosatlas.com/sitemap.xml): full URL index.
- [robots.txt](https://mythosatlas.com/robots.txt): crawl rules.

## API routes (not for general crawling)

`/api/*` routes are internal application APIs (search, analytics, CSP reports, quiz generation, Oracle AI). They are disallowed in robots.txt. Do not rely on them as stable public content APIs without maintainer agreement.

## Oracle (AI assistant)

The Oracle answers mythology questions using Anthropic Claude. When your question matches catalog entries, the API attaches snippets from the static encyclopedia (and key deity relationship edges), returns `X-Mythos-Grounding-Hits`, and may return `X-Mythos-Citations` (base64url JSON of `{ type, slug, title, path }[]`). Semantic similarity uses optional precomputed vectors in `src/data/oracle-embeddings.json` (generate via `pnpm --filter web run generate:embeddings` with `OPENAI_API_KEY`). The client sends UI `locale` (`en` | `es` | `fr` | `de`) for stopwords and answer language hints. Requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; optional Upstash Redis for rate limits — see `.env.example`.

## Editorial & trust signals

Structured entries are curated for consistency and cross-linking. The Sources page lists representative primary texts and references; About describes mission, scope, and how the project is maintained. Use Contact for corrections or substantive feedback.

## License / usage

Respect the site’s Terms and Privacy pages. For automated access, prefer sitemap and public HTML; avoid aggressive scraping of interactive or authenticated routes.
